text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Major public health authorities classify tobacco smoking as an established cause of lung cancer.","cited_pids":["smoking#6"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Cohort studies show lung cancer incidence rises with cumulative cigarette exposure in a dose response relationship.","cited_pids":["smoking#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Case control studies across many countries and decades report consistent and large effect sizes for smoking and lung cancer.","cited_pids":["smoking#4"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Lung cancer risk declines progressively after quitting smoking, with the decline tracking years since quitting.","cited_pids":["smoking#3"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Lung cancer rates fall in populations after sustained declines in smoking prevalence.","cited_pids":["smoking#2"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Tobacco smoke contains carcinogens that form DNA adducts in bronchial epithelium.","cited_pids":["smoking#1"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Animal experiments reproduce airway tumours from tobacco smoke exposure.","cited_pids":["smoking#5"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Second-hand smoke raises lung cancer risk in non-smokers.","cited_pids":["smoking#7"]}]}
